transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. Um... well, I'm just having trouble keeping my mind on things. I can't seem to stick with a task long enough to finish it anymore... even when it's important. 

I do computer support, and... I don't know, I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the same log entries three times. And I still don't know what they actually say. So... yeah. That's why I made the appointment.
When did you first notice that you were having trouble concentrating like this? Was it sudden, or did it come on gradually over time?

Um... I suppose it's been causing real trouble for... about a year and ten months. I guess you could say it was sudden. 

I was... well, I was fired from my old job back then. And... when that happened, I just lost the systems I had in place. The routines that used to keep me on track. It's just been pretty bad since then.
Besides the trouble concentrating, how has your mood been over this past year and ten months? Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?

Um... no, not really. I mean, getting fired wasn't great, obviously. But... I wouldn't say I've been depressed or hopeless. Just... frustrated with myself, mostly. Because I can't seem to get things done. But my mood is fine, I guess.
When you're doing something you really enjoy or find interesting—like a hobby or something you care about—do you have the same trouble focusing, or is it mainly with work-related tasks?

Um... no, it's... it's pretty much everything. I mean, I guess I already said this, but... I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even if it's something I care about. 

It's like what I was saying before about the network logs... I'll start looking at something, and then I just... I'm just reading the same thing over and over. It doesn't really matter what it is. It's just... hard to stay with it.
Before you got fired from your old job—back before that happened—did you have trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks?

Um... I suppose so. It's not exactly a new thing. 

My mother... well, she still jokes about my old grade school report cards. She says they always pointed out that I was bright, but... that I never stayed in my seat. And that I'd blurt out answers. I guess I also had a habit of losing my homework, even when I had actually done it. 

So... yeah. I guess I've always had some trouble with it.

You mentioned that before you got fired, you had some trouble concentrating even back in school. But when you compare how you were focusing at your old job—before you got fired—to how you're focusing now, would you say it's gotten noticeably worse, or is it about the same as it's always been?
Um... I don't know. I guess... maybe about the same. I'm not really sure. It's just... always been a problem.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F48.9 (Other specified nonorganic disorders) and F06.8 (Other specified mental disorders due to known physiological condition) based on clear childhood history of inattention, hyperactivity (not staying in seat, blurting out answers), and organizational difficulties (losing homework). These are cardinal features of ADHD. No evidence of anxiety disorder, somatic symptoms, or organic etiology. The concentration difficulties predate the job loss by years and appear lifelong, not secondary to recent stress or mood disorder.
